title: Constraint-Deletion Excitation Identity
statement:
Let \(\mathcal C=\{C_1,\dots,C_m\}\) be a finite CSP on a finite assignment
space \(\Omega\). For \(a\in\Omega\), let \(\nu(a)\) be the number of
violated constraints and let \(N_j=|\{a:\nu(a)=j\}|\). Then
\[
\sum_{i=1}^m |\operatorname{Sol}(\mathcal C-\{C_i\})|
  =mN_0+N_1.
\]

title: Higher Deletion Hierarchy
statement:
Under PG01, for \(0\le r\le m\),
\[
\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq[m]\\|S|=r}}
  |\operatorname{Sol}(\mathcal C-\{C_i:i\in S\})|
=
\sum_{a\in\Omega,\ \nu(a)\le r}
  \binom{m-\nu(a)}{r-\nu(a)}.
\]

title: Exact Constraint-Extension Repair Operator
statement:
Let \(\mathcal C=\{C_1,\dots,C_m\}\) be a finite CSP and let \(H\) be one
new constraint on the same variables. Define
\[
\rho(H\mid\mathcal C)
  =\min\{\nu_{\mathcal C}(a):a\models H\}.
\]
Then \(\rho(H\mid\mathcal C)\) is exactly the minimum number of old
constraints that must be deleted so that the augmented CSP
\(\mathcal C\cup\{H\}\) becomes satisfiable.

title: Finite-Domain Permutation-Cycle Realization
statement:
Let \(d\ge2\), \(n\ge7\), and let
\(\pi_0,\dots,\pi_{n-1}\in S_d\). There is a finite \(K_4\)-free graph
with stable parts
\[
P_i=\{p_i^a:a\in[d]\},
\]
whose consecutive fibers are the matchings
\[
p_i^a p_{i+1}^{\pi_i(a)}
\]
and whose distance-two fibers are the matchings
\[
p_i^a p_{i+2}^{\pi_{i+1}(\pi_i(a))}.
\]
Its realized triangle types are exactly the consecutive triples of parts,
and coherent sections are in bijection with the fixed points of
\[
\Pi=\pi_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\pi_0.
\]

title: Boundary-Projection Gluing Theorem
statement:
Let finite CSPs \(\mathcal C_1,\dots,\mathcal C_r\) have pairwise disjoint
internal variables and share exactly one boundary variable \(x\) with
domain \(D\). Let
\[
S_i=\{a\in D:\mathcal C_i\text{ has a solution with }x=a\}.
\]
Then their union is satisfiable if and only if
\[
\bigcap_{i=1}^r S_i\ne\varnothing.
\]
The number of global solutions is
\[
\sum_{a\in\cap_iS_i}\prod_i N_i(a),
\]
where \(N_i(a)\) counts solutions of \(\mathcal C_i\) with \(x=a\).

title: Permutation-Cycle Bouquet Theorem
statement:
Let permutation-cycle gadgets from PG04 share exactly one fiber variable
with common domain \(D\), while all other fiber variables are disjoint.
If \(\Pi_i\in S_D\) is the monodromy of gadget \(i\), then the bouquet has a
coherent section if and only if
\[
\bigcap_i \operatorname{Fix}(\Pi_i)\ne\varnothing.
\]
Its coherent sections are counted by that intersection, multiplied by any
independent attached-tree multiplicities.

title: First Pure Mixed Multicycle Obstruction
statement:
There is a finite \(K_4\)-free fiber-coherence system with incidence cycle
rank two such that each of its two cycle subsystems is coherent, every
relation is a bijection and every value is support-consistent, but the
union is incoherent.

title: Arbitrarily Large Minimal Monodromy Bouquets
No Helly Bound for Pure Monodromy Coherence
statement:
There is no finite Helly number for finite \(K_4\)-free fiber-coherence
systems even after restricting to bouquets of permutation cycles with all
values support-consistent.

title: Minimal-Incoherence Near-Solution Ledger
statement:
If a finite CSP with \(m\) constraints is inclusion-minimal incoherent,
then every constraint has a near-solution violating that constraint alone,
and
\[
N_1=\sum_{i=1}^m
  |\operatorname{Sol}(\mathcal C-\{C_i\})|
  \ge m.
\]

title: Cycle-Extension Repair Formula
statement:
Let a coherent permutation-cycle bouquet have fixed-set family
\(S_1,\dots,S_m\subseteq D\), and add one new cycle with fixed set \(T\).
The minimum number of old cycle blocks that must be deleted to restore
coherence is
\[
\min_{a\in T}|\{i:a\notin S_i\}|.
\]

title: Bouquet Deletion-Spectrum Identity
statement:
Let a permutation-cycle bouquet have fixed sets
\(S_1,\dots,S_m\subseteq D\). For \(0\le r\le m\),
\[
\sum_{\substack{I\subseteq[m]\\|I|=r}}
  \left|\bigcap_{i\notin I}S_i\right|
=
\sum_{a\in D}
  \binom{m-\nu(a)}{r-\nu(a)},
\]
where \(\nu(a)=|\{i:a\notin S_i\}|\), with the binomial coefficient read as
zero when \(r<\nu(a)\).

title: Exact Collision Penalty for Cycle Bouquets
statement:
For a permutation-cycle bouquet, incoherence is exactly the collision
condition
\[
\bigcap_i\operatorname{Fix}(\Pi_i)=\varnothing,
\]
and its block-deletion repair number is
\[
\min_{a\in D}|\{i:a\notin\operatorname{Fix}(\Pi_i)\}|.
\]

title: Cactus Block-Message Theorem
statement:
A finite fiber-coherence CSP whose incidence graph is a cactus is decidable
exactly by message passing on its block-cut tree. Tree blocks use CC12.
Every cycle block is first tree-absorbed by UC01 and then sends to each
articulation variable the exact set of boundary values extendable through
that cycle, computed by relation composition. The CSP is coherent if and
only if the root retains a value.

title: Cactus Obstruction Classification
statement:
Every finite incoherent fiber CSP with cactus incidence has an exact
certificate obtained by the PG14 block messages: either a tree/unicyclic
block emits an empty message, or nonempty child block messages have empty
intersection at an articulation variable. There is no further obstruction
mechanism inside the cactus class.

title: Pure Monodromy Cactus Universality
statement:
Every finite family of subsets \(S_i\subseteq D\) whose complements have
size other than one can be represented as the boundary-support family of a
\(K_4\)-free cactus of permutation-cycle blocks, because each such \(S_i\)
is the fixed-point set of a permutation of \(D\).

title: No Unclassified Core in the Cactus Regime
statement:
An inclusion-minimal finite incoherent fiber CSP not classified by the
forest, unicyclic, or cactus message theorems must contain a 2-connected
incidence block of cycle rank at least two.

title: Refined Finite-Fiber #595 Close Split
statement:
For a stable finite-fiber compression of a hypothetical Erdős #595 witness,
exactly one of the following occurs:
1. a finite cactus core with an explicit empty block/articulation message;
2. a finite minimal core containing a 2-connected incidence block of cycle
   rank at least two;
3. a full coherent section giving an exact uncountably chromatic
   Berge-\(C_3\)-free hypergraph compression.

title: Deletion-Debt Certificate for Minimal Cores
statement:
For every inclusion-minimal finite incoherent core with \(m\) constraints,
the complete vector
\[
\bigl(|\operatorname{Sol}(\mathcal C-C_i)|\bigr)_{i=1}^m
\]
is a positive integer deletion spectrum whose sum is the number of
assignments violating exactly one constraint. This spectrum is invariant
under CSP isomorphism and can be used as a first collision-classification
signature.

title: Biconnected Multicycle Collision Census Target
Core-Extension Slack
statement:
Let \(\mathcal C\) be a finite coherent fiber CSP and add one new
constraint \(H\). Define the extension slack
\[
\sigma(H\mid\mathcal C)=\rho(H\mid\mathcal C),
\]
with \(\rho\) from PG03. Then:
1. slack zero means the extension remains coherent;
2. slack one means deleting one old constraint is necessary and sufficient;
3. more generally slack is exactly the block-deletion distance from the new
   extension to coherence.

title: Collision-or-Slack Program for 2-Connected Cores
statement:
Build every minimal 2-connected multicycle core by adding constraints to a
coherent proper subcore. At each addition compute PG21 extension slack.
Determine whether every first intrinsic multicycle obstruction either:
1. is an overlap collision of two coherent cycle projections with disjoint
   boundary support; or
2. incurs a positive extension slack detectable before the final core.
A counterexample is a zero-slack growth path whose final step creates a new
intrinsic incoherence mechanism.
